correctness.rationale: The total cyclic-gap deficit from all threes is 2: either one gap 1 or two gaps 2. This precludes triple coverage and implies exactly two doubly covered sites. The closed-neighborhood operator A is injective because a kernel vector is 3-periodic and gcd(3,n)=1. Under multiplication by 3 inverse, the first gap type gives separation m-1 up to reversal, and the second gives separations j+m-1, 1<=j<=m-1. The counts agree (n(m+1)/2), so the map is onto. In both directions a transformed +1 move is the coverage change delta_(i+2)-delta_(i-1)=A(delta_(i+1)-delta_i); injectivity recovers a legal original slide. The lifted integer strip is L1-geodesic by monotone paths through a feasible coordinatewise minimum. All lifts of a target form one orbit under (a,b)->(b,a+n). A q nearest to the sum difference divided by n yields a sum residual <=floor(n/2) and gap residual <=m<=floor(n/2); other q cannot improve it (their sum residual alone is at least floor(n/2)). Standard-lift sums differ by less than 2n, so this nearest q is among the stated five. From every state one may shift the target sum by floor(n/2), adjusting its gap by one if needed for parity; all target lifts then have sum residual at least floor(n/2). Boundary pairs have exactly two legal moves and interior pairs four, including the n=4 case. This proves the exact distance, eccentricity and census, independently of any finite test. Replay: python3 /workspace/branches/independent_checks.py 1; independent bitmask enumeration and graph breadth layers at n=4,7,10,13,16 agreed for all 5,514 ordered pairs. The frozen script was inspected, not executed; its recorded larger finite run is corroboration only.
